item.text: {"facts":[{"source_id":"SRC-74b9009ff2271f55","start_unit":5,"end_unit":9,"fact_summary":"The CNDH reports 564 complaints involving migrant children and adolescents between January 2021 and October 2022, issued recommendations concerning violations of their best interests, and concluded that legislative and policy advances existed but DIF institutions still required greater budgetary, staffing, procedural support, and training.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.7","3B.9","3B.10","6B.1","6B.2","6B.3","6B.4","6B.5","6B.9","6B.10","8B.8","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The evidence concerns 2021-2022 and institutional conditions inherited or continuing into 2023; it does not establish López Obrador's personal direction of each measure.","ruler_attribution":"The report evaluates Mexican federal and subnational authorities, including institutions operating under the federal administration, rather than attributing every finding personally to López Obrador.","limitations":["The report does not provide a complete 2023 outcome assessment.","Recommendations and institutional findings do not by themselves establish personal intent or individual responsibility."]},{"source_id":"SRC-74b9009ff2271f55","start_unit":19,"end_unit":21,"fact_summary":"Amnesty International, as summarized by the CNDH, reported excessive force, arbitrary detention, illegal returns, kidnappings, and homicides affecting migrants; authorities detained large numbers in overcrowded facilities despite hygiene deficiencies, including children despite the legal prohibition, and thousands of unaccompanied minors were returned without their best interests being considered.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.5","3B.6","3B.7","3B.9","3B.10","7B.2","8B.6","8B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The summarized Amnesty evidence primarily concerns 2021 and is relevant as a baseline and unresolved implementation problem for 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The findings concern Mexican migration and security authorities; the source does not assign personal responsibility to López Obrador.","limitations":["The CNDH summary notes a discrepancy between Amnesty's detention total and the official bulletin total.","The evidence is not a comprehensive assessment of all migration operations."]},{"source_id":"SRC-74b9009ff2271f55","start_unit":34,"end_unit":41,"fact_summary":"CNDH recommendations documented repeated violations involving migrants and children: deportation of Haitian refugee applicants without non-refoulement assessment; disproportionate National Guard and migration-agent force against migrants and children; failure to promptly notify protection authorities or transfer children to appropriate shelters; overcrowding and inadequate facilities; delayed or inadequate food, health care, and protection; and physical violence against a Haitian family.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.5","3B.6","3B.7","3B.9","3B.10","7B.2","7B.7","8B.6","8B.8","8B.9","8B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The recommendations concern incidents from 2021-2022, providing evidence of implementation failures relevant to the 2023 inherited administrative context.","ruler_attribution":"The findings concern INM, National Guard, SSPC, and DIF authorities; the report does not show that López Obrador personally ordered each violation.","limitations":["The source records recommendations and verified institutional violations, but not the subsequent completeness of remedies or disciplinary action.","Several findings concern state DIF systems outside direct federal control."]},{"source_id":"SRC-74b9009ff2271f55","start_unit":46,"end_unit":54,"fact_summary":"Mexico established a 2021-2024 national child-protection program, a model assigning SNDIF and protection procuracies responsibility for migrant children, open or non-detention social assistance centers, multidisciplinary procedures, humanitarian visitor status, protection plans, interagency coordination, and a national mobility registry launched in October 2022 with gradual national implementation and international support.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.4","3B.5","3B.7","3B.9","3B.10","6B.1","6B.2","6B.3","6B.4","6B.5","6B.9","8B.1","8B.2","8B.3","8B.5","8B.6","8B.9","8B.10"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The institutional measures were adopted before or during 2022 and could operate in 2023; the source does not independently verify their 2023 implementation quality.","ruler_attribution":"These were federal policies and institutions under the López Obrador administration, but implementation was shared with state and municipal authorities and international partners.","limitations":["The registry began with information from Chiapas and was intended to scale gradually.","Formal rules and launch of an information system do not establish nationwide compliance."]},{"source_id":"SRC-74b9009ff2271f55","start_unit":61,"end_unit":71,"fact_summary":"DIF systems reported growth from 39 to 41 migrant-child assistance centers and from 1,757 to 2,611 places between 2020 and 2021, with spending rising from 233.3 million to 541.8 million pesos; however, systems served only 59.9% of 77,608 children referred in 2021, many states reported shortages of infrastructure, staff, supplies, and funds, data were incomplete, and about half transferred people to alternative shelters when capacity was exceeded.","question_ids":["3B.7","3B.9","3B.10","5B.6","5B.7","6B.1","6B.2","6B.3","6B.4","6B.5","6B.6","6B.9","6B.10","8B.2","8B.3","8B.5","8B.6","8B.7","8B.8","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The quantitative comparison is for 2020-2021, relevant to the capacity and implementation baseline entering 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The spending and capacity figures concern federal and state DIF systems; the source does not isolate López Obrador's personal budgetary decisions.","limitations":["The report identifies inconsistencies and missing fields in state submissions.","The coverage percentage does not show what happened to all children not reported as served."]},{"source_id":"SRC-74b9009ff2271f55","start_unit":57,"end_unit":61,"fact_summary":"A SIPINNA consultation with 162 migrant children and adolescents found mixed experiences: some reported kind treatment and adequate shelters, but nearly half of adolescents did not remember speaking with authorities or receiving medical review, 62% said their migration status was not explained, 75% said their opinion was not requested, and children reported unaddressed bullying and distress.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.4","3B.7","3B.8","3B.9","3B.10","6B.2","6B.3","6B.5","6B.8","8B.6","8B.7","8B.8","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The consultation reports experiences in the route before 2023 and is relevant to implementation quality entering the target year.","ruler_attribution":"The evidence concerns the operation of the national protection route by Mexican authorities, without proving personal conduct by López Obrador.","limitations":["The sample included accompanied children in civil-society shelters and excluded unaccompanied children and DIF-run centers, creating selection bias.","Reported perceptions do not establish the frequency of every condition nationally."]},{"source_id":"SRC-74b9009ff2271f55","start_unit":102,"end_unit":108,"fact_summary":"CNDH concluded that the protection route had problems at entry and best-interests stages, protocols were not consistently implemented, records omitted basic demographic and health information, capacity and staffing were inadequate, refugee data diverged sharply from COMAR data, and there was no uniform guarantee that state instruments or multidisciplinary teams protected children's rights.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.5","3B.7","3B.9","3B.10","6B.2","6B.3","6B.4","6B.5","6B.9","6B.10","7B.2","8B.5","8B.6","8B.7","8B.8","8B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"These are the CNDH's observations on 2021-2022 systems and identify unresolved implementation weaknesses relevant to 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The observations concern institutions across federal and state levels; they do not assign all failures personally to López Obrador.","limitations":["The report is an oversight assessment rather than a complete causal evaluation of presidential policy.","Some conclusions are explicitly framed as presumptions based on incomplete data."]},{"source_id":"SRC-74b9009ff2271f55","start_unit":109,"end_unit":114,"fact_summary":"The CNDH proposed a national standard, at least one migrant-child center in every state, dedicated funding and staffing, professionalization, harmonized protocols, public semiannual mobility reporting, stronger registration, legal representation, and supervision of all assistance centers.","question_ids":["3B.4","3B.7","6B.1","6B.2","6B.3","6B.4","6B.5","6B.9","8B.1","8B.2","8B.5","8B.6","8B.8","8B.10"],"polarity":"context","period_fit":"These are proposed corrective actions issued for future implementation after the 2021-2022 assessment, relevant to unresolved 2023 policy needs.","ruler_attribution":"The proposals were directed to SNDIF, state DIF systems, protection procuracies, and SIPINNA, not to López Obrador personally.","limitations":["Proposals are not evidence that the recommended measures were enacted or funded in 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-796f2a8cf19b045b","start_unit":4,"end_unit":7,"fact_summary":"The UN report describes close coordination with Mexico's federal government and highlights reported progress between 2018 and 2022: 5.1 million fewer people in poverty, reduced inequality, higher minimum wages, a universal older-adult pension, and social programs; it also notes persistent extreme and indigenous poverty, gender inequality, violence against women, unsafe water and sanitation, high homicide and disappearance levels, and unprecedented irregular migration in 2023.","question_ids":["3B.6","3B.7","3B.10","4B.10","5B.1","5B.8","5B.10","6B.1","6B.2","6B.3","6B.6","6B.10","8B.7","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The report covers outcomes through circa 2023, while some poverty and inequality figures cover 2018-2022 and therefore provide a recent trajectory rather than a strictly 2023-only result.","ruler_attribution":"The UN describes national outcomes and government collaboration but does not attribute all changes solely to López Obrador or distinguish federal from subnational and external contributions.","limitations":["The report is a UN program-results document and not an independent causal evaluation of presidential policy.","Several indicators are national aggregates and do not establish distribution across all groups."]},{"source_id":"SRC-796f2a8cf19b045b","start_unit":7,"end_unit":10,"fact_summary":"The UN report identifies mixed development performance: poverty and inequality improved, but extreme poverty remained 7.1%, indigenous poverty 65.2%, gender inequality and violence remained high, safe water and adequate wastewater treatment declined, homicide and disappearances remained elevated, and 2023 irregular migration was 2.5 times the 2021 level.","question_ids":["3B.6","3B.7","3B.10","5B.8","5B.10","6B.2","6B.3","6B.6","6B.10","8B.7","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The evidence combines 2015-2023 trends with 2023 conditions and is relevant to end-period assessment.","ruler_attribution":"The report evaluates national conditions during the administration but does not establish that López Obrador caused each trend.","limitations":["Some indicators use different endpoint years, including 2015-2019, 2015-2021, or 2016-2022.","The report does not provide a counterfactual."]},{"source_id":"SRC-796f2a8cf19b045b","start_unit":9,"end_unit":14,"fact_summary":"In 2023 the UN implemented 261 initiatives nationwide and revised its cooperation plan for 2023-2025; projects addressed equality, social protection, education, mobility, food security, resilience, and territorial planning. Reported outputs included more than 80% of state development plans aligned with the Agenda 2030, 130 municipalities starting urban plans, and substantial education, nutrition, shelter, and migrant-support interventions, while shelter demand exceeded capacity in some areas by more than 300%.","question_ids":["3B.7","3B.9","3B.10","5B.6","5B.7","6B.1","6B.2","6B.3","6B.4","6B.5","6B.6","6B.9","6B.10","8B.1","8B.2","8B.3","8B.5","8B.6","8B.7","8B.8","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"These are 2023 implementation and output findings, but many interventions were conducted by UN agencies with government and non-government partners.","ruler_attribution":"The report records cooperation with the Mexican government, including federal and local authorities, but does not attribute UN outputs solely to López Obrador.","limitations":["Reported outputs are program-level and do not establish national causal impact.","Some projects were implemented by subnational governments, civil society, or international agencies."]},{"source_id":"SRC-796f2a8cf19b045b","start_unit":13,"end_unit":14,"fact_summary":"In 2023 UNICEF, UN agencies, and partners supported migrant children through education in emergencies for 13,561 children, teacher training, protection-route planning in ten states, more than 6,400 interventions in 204 shelters, and a national strategy that trained over 800 health professionals and reached more than 250,000 children and pregnant women; the report simultaneously describes shelter overload and improvised camps.","question_ids":["3B.7","3B.9","3B.10","6B.2","6B.3","6B.4","6B.6","6B.9","6B.10","8B.5","8B.6","8B.7","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The evidence is directly from 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The report identifies collaboration with Mexican federal and state institutions, but the documented services were delivered largely through UN agencies, civil society, and partner institutions.","limitations":["The figures measure program reach, not total national coverage or outcomes.","Shelter capacity pressures indicate continuing unmet need despite interventions."]},{"source_id":"SRC-796f2a8cf19b045b","start_unit":16,"end_unit":18,"fact_summary":"The UN reported 2023 labor and inclusion initiatives: more than 35,000 refugees and asylum seekers accessed formal employment through the Local Integration Program, 90% of participants reported formal employment and children's school integration, more than 8,700 women gained skills through a multi-year program, and rural women's networks and value-chain projects expanded economic opportunities.","question_ids":["5B.1","5B.4","5B.8","5B.10","6B.3","6B.10","8B.6","8B.7","8B.10"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The evidence includes outcomes reported in 2023, though some initiatives began before 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The programs involved Mexican federal, state, and local authorities with UN, civil-society, and private partners; the source does not isolate presidential contribution.","limitations":["Some reported employment outcomes are self-reported or program-specific.","The evidence does not show national incidence or long-term durability."]},{"source_id":"SRC-796f2a8cf19b045b","start_unit":17,"end_unit":19,"fact_summary":"The UN reported that Mexico's labor reform and T-MEC were accompanied by strengthened labor institutions, review and validation of more than 80,000 collective contracts, and training for labor officials; it also documented 3.7 million children in child labor and a 2023 national pact based on survey evidence to prevent and eliminate child labor.","question_ids":["3B.7","5B.4","5B.6","5B.7","5B.8","5B.10","6B.3","6B.10","8B.2","8B.6","8B.7","8B.8"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The institutional reform and child-labor pact evidence is reported for the recent period through 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The reforms involved the federal government, state governments, labor institutions, unions, and international organizations; the report does not establish personal presidential authorship of each measure.","limitations":["The existence of a pact and contract review does not establish elimination of child labor or full enforcement.","The 3.7 million figure derives from the 2022 survey reported in 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-796f2a8cf19b045b","start_unit":22,"end_unit":23,"fact_summary":"In response to Hurricane Otis in 2023, the UN worked with federal, state, and municipal governments, civil society, and private actors through eight thematic worktables covering protection, nutrition, education, shelter, health, recovery, water and sanitation, and communications, transitioning toward reconstruction and resilience.","question_ids":["3B.7","3B.9","3B.10","6B.2","6B.3","6B.6","6B.9","6B.10","8B.5","8B.6","8B.8","8B.9","8B.10"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The evidence is directly from the 2023 Otis response.","ruler_attribution":"The report describes coordinated work with the Mexican federal government and other actors, but does not establish López Obrador's personal decisions or the adequacy of the full national response.","limitations":["The report describes coordination and assistance, not a complete assessment of recovery outcomes or distributional equity.","External humanitarian support was a substantial component."]},{"source_id":"SRC-796f2a8cf19b045b","start_unit":24,"end_unit":27,"fact_summary":"The UN reported 2023 institutional and rights initiatives including 80 strengthened laws on gender violence and feminicide, training for 8,400 public servants, a port container-control unit to detect illicit flows, a national anti-smuggling strategy, refugee-system digitization that increased COMAR capacity fourfold from 2018 to 2023, and responses to displacement and protection cases; it also corroborated the killings or disappearances of nine journalists and 21 human-rights defenders in 2023.","question_ids":["1B.6","2B.5","3B.1","3B.2","3B.3","3B.4","3B.7","3B.8","3B.10","4B.3","4B.6","4B.9","6B.5","6B.8","7B.2","7B.6","8B.2","8B.5","8B.6","8B.7","8B.8","8B.9","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The evidence is directly from 2023, with the COMAR comparison spanning 2018-2023.","ruler_attribution":"The report records actions by Mexican federal and subnational institutions in cooperation with UN agencies; it does not attribute all improvements or harms personally to López Obrador.","limitations":["The report does not establish whether strengthened laws were uniformly enforced.","The journalist and defender findings are not a complete national violence dataset."]},{"source_id":"SRC-796f2a8cf19b045b","start_unit":26,"end_unit":28,"fact_summary":"In 2023 Mexico received more than 140,000 asylum applications, a record that saturated the under-resourced asylum system; UN support expanded COMAR capacity and digital case management, while authorities and partners developed displacement responses, protection measures, and a national anti-smuggling strategy.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.4","3B.7","3B.9","3B.10","6B.2","6B.3","6B.5","6B.6","6B.9","6B.10","8B.5","8B.6","8B.7","8B.8","8B.9","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The evidence is directly from 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The asylum and migration institutions were Mexican public bodies operating during López Obrador's administration, while capacity-building was supported by ACNUR and other partners.","limitations":["The report does not state how many applications received timely, accurate, or favorable decisions.","The record of saturation limits conclusions about effective nationwide service delivery."]},{"source_id":"SRC-796f2a8cf19b045b","start_unit":29,"end_unit":30,"fact_summary":"The UN reported close coordination with the Mexican Foreign Ministry and government through the 2020-2025 cooperation framework, including more than 4,800 interventions for people in mobility and interagency emergency and accountability mechanisms; it also reported training on protection from sexual exploitation and abuse and public campaigns supporting human rights and press freedom.","question_ids":["2B.6","3B.4","3B.8","3B.9","4B.3","4B.6","7B.6","7B.7","8B.5","8B.8","8B.9"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The evidence concerns 2023 coordination and oversight arrangements.","ruler_attribution":"The report describes cooperation with the Mexican government and Foreign Ministry but does not establish López Obrador's personal role in each mechanism.","limitations":["Most mechanisms are described from the UN's institutional perspective.","The report does not independently evaluate the government's compliance with every accountability recommendation."]},{"source_id":"SRC-796f2a8cf19b045b","start_unit":31,"end_unit":33,"fact_summary":"The UN's 2023 evaluation identified collaboration, interagency coordination, and emergency capacity as strengths, but emphasized the need for sustained private-sector partnership, community-level work, and stronger inclusion of youth, disabled people, older adults, Indigenous and Afro-descendant populations; the 2024 priorities included continued work on care systems, violence monitoring, justice, gender violence, mobility, and external evaluation.","question_ids":["3B.7","3B.10","4B.10","5B.7","5B.10","6B.3","6B.5","6B.9","6B.10","8B.7","8B.8","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The evaluation and lessons learned are for 2023, while the priorities are forward-looking and not evidence of completed 2023 action.","ruler_attribution":"The assessment concerns the UN-Mexico cooperation framework and national partners, not solely presidential performance.","limitations":["Forward-looking priorities cannot be treated as completed outcomes.","The evaluation does not provide a counterfactual or comprehensive audit of Mexican government policy."]}],"documents_with_no_material_fact":[],"batch_limitations":["The supplied documents concern institutional and national conditions rather than López Obrador's personal conduct in every domain.","No supplied document provides material evidence on nuclear-risk governance, nuclear or conventional arms-control decisions, or most integrity-specific questions concerning personal assets, conflicts of interest, appointments for self-dealing, truthfulness, or obstruction of personal accountability.","The first document primarily covers 2021-2022 and is used as inherited or continuing implementation context for 2023; the second covers 2023 but frequently reports joint UN-government or subnational initiatives, limiting personal attribution.","Facts are not scores and should not be interpreted as chapter judgments."]}
